data.title: Middle East Eye: Drone that killed two Italians in Kuwait was Iranian-made, says Italy's foreign minister
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Drone that killed two Italians in Kuwait was Iranian-made, says Italy's foreign minister
The drone used in the attack on Kuwait that killed two Italians was manufactured in Iran, Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on Friday.
In an interview with the Italian press, Tajani said: "According to the investigations carried out by the Kuwaitis, the drone was manufactured in Iran."
The attack on Thursday also injured two other people.
It drew condemnation from many countries, and some, including Syria and Saudi Arabia, blamed Iran for it.
Meanwhile, Iran has denied launching the drone, with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi calling the incident "suspicious".
"The Iranians say it was not launched from Iranian territory, but, as you know, Iran's proxies, all of Iran's allies, have Iranian-made drones," Tajani told press.
"There will be investigations, and the Iranians have said they are ready to participate in a commission of inquiry alongside the Italians and Kuwaitis," he added.

In a post on X, he said the second meeting of the Political and Defence Strategic Committee of the Mecca Defence Alliance "affirms our countries’ unified position and active role in addressing the current situation and the close cooperation and coordination it requires to strengthen security and stability".
On the sidelines of the meeting, Khalid bin Salman held talks with Turkey's Minister of National Defence, Yasar Guler.
"We commended the meeting’s outcomes and stressed the importance of continuing to strengthen and develop military and defence cooperation to serve our shared interests and achieve security and stability," he said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli defence minister rejects army chief's call to detain violent settlers, report says
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Israeli defence minister rejects army chief's call to detain violent settlers, report says
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has rejected a new request from military chief of staff Eyal Zamir to authorise administrative detention orders against Israeli settlers involved in attacks against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, Kan reported.
Zamir told Katz at a security consultation on Thursday that further steps were needed amid rising settler violence, and called for administrative detention and restraining orders against perpetrators, the report said.
Administrative detention allows suspects to be held indefinitely without charge or trial. It is widely used against Palestinians, including children, but Katz halted its use against Jewish Israelis in November 2024. He has, in fact, repeatedly boasted of doing so, while expanding its use against Palestinians.
Dozens of restraining orders, which bar individuals from parts of the West Bank, are awaiting Shin Bet approval, according to Kan. Channel 12 reported that 70 people suspected of involvement in such attacks were arrested in recent weeks, but Israeli courts released all of them without indictments.
Shin Bet chief David Zini, who belongs to the Orthodox nationalist Hardal camp, has consistently objected to movement bans. He has been accused of undermining the agency's unit tasked with tackling settler violence.
A surge in Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank this year has been condemned globally. (AFP)

data.title: Middle East Eye: US activist returning from West Bank tour detained by Israeli police, UCPiP says
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
US activist returning from West Bank tour detained by Israeli police, UCPiP says
Israeli police have detained Mel Duncan, co-founder of Unarmed Civilian Protection in Palestine (UCPiP), as he was returning to Tel Aviv after a tour of the occupied West Bank, the organisation said in a statement on X.
A US citizen from St. Paul, Minnesota, and a longtime advocate for nonviolence and civilian protection, Mel was not engaged in any illegal activity, UCPiP said.
"He was travelling on a bus full of Israeli citizens returning from a tour of the West Bank and heading towards Tel Aviv when Israeli police stopped the bus, held it for approximately an hour, and confiscated his passport. Mel was the only passenger detained," the statement read.
He is currently being held at Ma’ale Adumim police station, and the grounds for his detention remain unclear, the statement added.
His lawyer has requested urgent diplomatic intervention to ensure he is questioned tonight rather than spending two nights in detention. The organisation also urged the US Embassy in Israel, elected representatives and the international community to intervene and secure Mel's release.

data.title: Middle East Eye: UKMTO says five percent of ships attacked since 17 Aug sunk or lost
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
UKMTO says five percent of ships attacked since 17 Aug sunk or lost
About 5 percent of vessels reported attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz have been confirmed lost or sunk since the Iran-US Memorandum of Understanding expired on 17 August, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).
Roughly 43 percent of ships in these incidents appear on the non-compliance list of the Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA), which was set up by Iran in May, UKMTO said in its weekly overview.
The PGSA blacklists ships it accuses of breaking its Hormuz transit rules, threatening fines, detention or confiscation. Its list passed 120 vessels in October.
According to the weekly overview, three tankers were struck by unknown projectiles within about 17 minutes on 22 November while heading east through the Strait of Hormuz. All three continued their voyages.
UKMTO documented 10 incidents in the week to 25 November, seven of them in the Strait of Hormuz.
Combined transits remain roughly 65 percent below pre-conflict levels, with 166 outbound and 173 inbound crossings last week. About 70 percent were energy carriers, and more vessels are using the southern route.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran's navy commander says country's maritime ports 'fully operational'
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Iran's navy commander says country's maritime ports 'fully operational'
Iran’s Navy commander, Rear Admiral Shahram Irani, has said the country's maritime ports were fully operational despite the "enemy's attempts to disrupt the economy", Mehr news agency reported, citing the state broadcaster, Irib.
Irani said the United States was forced to retreat to the Arabian Sea and northern Indian Ocean and warned that any further military operations "will push American forces out of the region and back to US shores".
He stated that a naval blockade is traditionally imposed before a war to pressure an adversary, but announcing one during an ongoing war amounts to an admission "that the enemy has failed" to achieve its military objectives, the report said.
“The enemy has not reached any of its malicious goals,” he said, warning that there would be "no geographical limits in confronting the enemy".
He said Iran would launch not just one, but a series of operations in case of "any mistake".

data.author: Hilal Saki

Morning update

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iranian tennis player withdraws from ITF match to avoid Israeli opponent
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Iranian tennis player withdraws from ITF match to avoid Israeli opponent
Iranian tennis player Ali Yazdani has withdrawn from the men’s doubles quarterfinals of the ITF World Tennis Tour in Antalya, Turkey, to avoid playing an opponent from Israel, according to Irna.
Yazdani and his Russian partner Egor Khotchenkov were considered the leading contenders for the doubles title. They were scheduled to face an Austrian-Israeli pair in the quarterfinals on Friday.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli gunfire kills Palestinian child in Gaza's Khan Younis
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Israeli gunfire kills Palestinian child in Gaza's Khan Younis
A Palestinian child was wounded by Israeli forces' gunfire early Saturday in the city of Khan Younis, south of the Gaza Strip, Wafa reported.
Israeli forces continued artillery shelling and machine-gun fire from tanks, military vehicles, helicopters and naval vessels, targeting various areas across southern, central and northern Gaza, the report added.
